answer: The hobby I'd like to talk about is reading, which has been a part of my life since childhood. It started when my parents gave me story books, and I quickly became [[hooked]]. I still remember my father bringing home Bengali adventure stories from the market, and I would read them again and again until the pages were falling out. These days I read almost every evening before bed, mostly non-fiction and the occasional novel, and on Fridays I sometimes manage a couple of hours with a cup of tea. What I love about it is how it allows me to escape into different worlds and [[broaden]] my knowledge at the same time. Reading is also wonderfully [[therapeutic]]; after a stressful day, losing myself in a good book helps me unwind completely. I tend to switch between history, biographies and books about psychology, so there is always something new to look forward to. Beyond entertainment, it has noticeably improved my vocabulary and the way I express myself, which really helps in my job, since I spend a lot of time writing to students and universities. Honestly, in an age dominated by screens, I think reading is an increasingly [[underrated]] pleasure. It costs very little yet offers enormous rewards. I always keep a book on my bedside table, and I feel slightly restless if I go too long without one. Looking back, those simple story books were a truly [[formative]] influence on me, and reading is a hobby I hope to keep for the rest of my life.

followUps.q: Do you prefer printed books or e-books?
followUps.answer: Printed books, without a doubt. I like the feel of the paper and being able to scribble notes in the margins. I do read on my phone when travelling, but it never feels quite the same.

followUps.q: Would you like your family to read more?
followUps.answer: My younger sister already reads a lot, so she doesn't need encouragement. I'd love my nephew in Dhaka to develop the habit, though, so I always bring him a colourful picture book when I visit.
